about: Born, Not Made, simplified version after the sketch of 21 November 2026. Frame: x toward the opening, y port, z up, meters; origin on the docking plane, on the inner floor (the tank floor is 3 mm lower).

stages.name: Dock
stages.text: The tail docks to the gel chamber in the dry tank: three disc magnets pull the thin docking ring onto the seal.

stages.name: Unfold, gel
stages.text: The arm unfolds and injects the gel: 5.4 L at 0.1 L per minute. This is the first fill; the gel then stays in the bowl from birth to birth. Then the water comes in.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The suction cup picks the electronics kit once and places the kit in the gel, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change at the rack in the tail: suction cup off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release).

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the folded newborn around the kit: 40 m of bead, 0.08 L of Dragon Skin 10 NV.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, pneumatic module on.

stages.name: Air in, nose up
stages.text: The nozzle enters the valve. Air pushes the trapped gel out of the folds, the newborn floats up in the gel, and the arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises above the lip.

stages.name: Push while inflating
stages.text: The arm steers the tail end from above and pushes; the newborn slides over the lip, and each segment opens outside. No contractions.

stages.name: Hold and fill
stages.text: The arm holds, the newborn fills to full size, the nozzle lets go.

stages.name: Float
stages.text: The newborn floats in the water: gravity, buoyancy, drag, a damped settling.

stages.name: Swim
stages.text: The newborn takes ballast, sits lower and swims on two jets.

notes: The tail is set down behind the gel chamber in the dry tank and slid forward; three magnets close the last millimeters and press the seal.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, between the two parked modules, over the gel bowl. The base does not move.
Gel comes through the line on the arm; the arm moves the outlet over three fill points.
With the gel in, the tank is filled with water to 88 mm. The gel stands higher than the water at the seam.
The bare arm folds back between the two parked modules in the tail. The pneumatic module waits there with the cup on the kit.
The bare arm turns in behind the module.
The quick release slides onto the module and clicks.
Vacuum on: the cup holds the kit.
The module slides forward out of the fork; the kit moves through the gel.
The kit moves through the gel to the centerline.
The kit is carried forward and up, out of the tail, over the print seat.
The kit goes straight down through the gel onto the three seat bumps.
Vacuum off: the kit stays on the seat, the cup lifts clear.
Tool change in the tail: the pneumatic module goes back into the fork.
The pin on the fork presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm turns 48 degrees, behind the modules, to the print needle.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle slides forward out of the fork, through the gel.
The needle goes forward through the gel to the kit.
The folded newborn is printed around the kit, layer by layer, in clear silicone.
The silicone cures in the gel (75 minutes at room temperature). The print needle goes back to the rack in the tail.
The pneumatic module is back on the arm: the same nozzle that held the kit now carries the air.
The nozzle goes to the valve on the tail end of the newborn.
Air at 450 Pa pushes the gel out of the folds through the vent in the nose; the drained newborn rises 30 mm and floats in the gel.
The nozzle presses the tail end down in the gel: the nose rises above the lip of the opening.
Push while inflating: every segment opens once the segment is out of the opening. All the air comes through the nozzle on the arm.
At full reach the arm holds the nozzle in the valve while the rest of the air goes in; the skin stretches by a quarter and the creases pull smooth.
The nozzle lets go. The newborn floats free, rocks and settles; the arm parks the module and folds back into the tail.
The kit pumps take water into the belly pocket until the jets are under water; the newborn swims a slow turn on two jets.

checks.name: Tail prints in one piece on the H2S: 286 x 314 x 336 mm of 340 x 320 x 340
Gel chamber prints in one piece: 240 x 314 x 336 mm
Folded arm ends 65 mm behind the docking plane; tower top 11 mm under the tail roof

Rack, tools and kit store are in the tail print: the modules hang 150 mm ahead of the arm axis, 4 mm behind the docking plane, with the head 8 mm above the gel and the stems in the gel; no tool crosses a wall
The print needle reaches all 1140 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges
The parts dock and take the gel in the dry tank. With the gel in and 88 mm of water, the tail weighs 8.0 kg against 6.5 kg of buoyancy (the 5 mm steel plate under the arm base is the ballast)
The filled gel chamber rests on the floor: weight 4.6 kg, buoyancy 3.1 kg
Without gel the parts would lift in the water (together 7.4 kg against 9.6 kg of buoyancy), so the gel goes in before the water, and the bowl is not emptied under water

The lip of the opening is 22 mm above the water and 3 mm above the gel. The docking seam crosses the gel bowl under water, so the ring carries a silicone cord pressed by the magnets (161 N). With the gel in, the gel is 186 Pa above the water at the seam, and a gel with a yield stress of 25 Pa does not flow through a gap under 1.1 mm on the 4 mm ring
The gel stays in the bowl between births: 5.37 L in the bowl, about 19 mL leave with each newborn (0.4 percent); the level falls 0.6 mm a birth, topped up through the arm
The lip is 3 mm above the gel surface; the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm, and the folded print has already raised the level before the push
Every part of the tail sits inside two printed pockets beside the arm; the deepest a part reaches through a pocket wall is 0.0 mm
Energy for one cycle about 25 Wh (the Raspberry Pi 5 takes a third); the battery (six 18650 cells) holds 54 Wh: margin 2.1. The inflator runs on a battery of its own
Silicone: the two bores hold 96 mL, one newborn takes 75 mL

Air: the inflator of the artist fills a size 7 basketball (7.6 L, 55 kPa) in 35 s, which is 7.1 L of free air per minute; the newborn (11.3 L at 1.3 kPa) fills in about 96 s. The inflator must stop at 1.3 kPa: the preset of a tire inflator may not go that low (open question)
Open question: the inflator gives no vacuum. Proposed vacuum source for the suction cup: one micro pump (ZR370-02PM, 55 kPa stall vacuum), drawn in the pocket
Open question: the three way valve of the artist is a manual stopcock. A micro servo on the lever, or the lever set by hand before the cycle
Every pose of the timeline is inside the official joint ranges (base -24 to 24, J1 0 to 58, J2 3 to 85 degrees)
Suction: the 15 mm cup holds 2.9 N (half of the 55 kPa stall vacuum of the proposed micro pump, 60 percent seal), the kit weighs 1.05 N: margin 2.8
Payload while carrying the kit: 167 g of 500 g
Force of the nozzle on the valve stays under the payload: peak 1.96 N of 4.91 N
The rubber ball valve grips the needle against the largest upward pull: 1.37 N of about 2 N (estimate, to bench test)
The newborn leaves through the center of the opening
checks.value: the axis passes 60 mm below the center: the body rides on the lip, on the centerline

checks.name: Folds can be printed: story pitch 5.0 mm with one valley, pleat walls 7.1 mm apart at mid depth (limit: 1.2 mm wall plus 2 mm of gel)
Kresling stories are bistable with a barrier strain of 3.1 percent, far under the 25 percent stretch of the skin
Stretch 1.25 stays under the limit point of the membrane (1.38) and uses 4 percent of the 663 percent elongation at break
Full size 395 x 280 mm against the gel chamber 240 x 314 x 336 mm: 165 percent of the length, 89 percent of the width
The newborn floats upright: metacentric height 34 mm dry, 76 mm with ballast
Draft 28 mm dry; 0.45 kg of water in the belly pocket puts the jets 45 mm under water
The motion settles: pitch rate in the last three seconds under 0.02 degrees per second; deepest contact at the lip 0.00 mm
Per frame penetration test over 2304 frames: deepest overlap of any pair 0.00 mm (limit 1 mm)
UNS 150U: the parent body (526 mm long, 336 mm tall) and the newborn (395 mm) in the 1470 mm inner length, with a swim run of 886 mm; water 64 L, about 198 kg filled

deriv.name: Arm base
deriv.value: fixed, 162 mm behind the docking plane, on a 5 mm steel plate on the tail floor
deriv.why: The folded DexArm reaches 97 mm ahead of its axis. Ahead of the folded arm the tail needs 65 mm more for the rack: the modules hang 150 mm ahead of the axis, the nearest the arm can hold a tool. From there the tool tip reaches 393 mm from the axis at the height of the print.

deriv.name: Tail
deriv.why: The folded arm stands 314 mm tall on a 5 mm steel plate; the roof is 11 mm above the tower. Nothing stands behind the arm any more: the rear wall is 57 mm behind the folded arm, the least the folded arm and its sweep allow (closest approach 5 mm in the test). The tail is 97 mm shorter than the first version. One print on the H2S (340 x 320 x 340 mm), 54, 6 and 4 mm clear of the build volume.

deriv.name: Print needle
deriv.why: The head stays above the gel (92 mm deep over the lowest printed point) while the tip prints the lowest layer.

deriv.name: Printed newborn
deriv.why: With the needle hanging 122 mm below the wrist, the arm reaches from 206 mm to 393 mm from its axis at the axis of the print, and from 237 mm to 371 mm at the top of the print. The 150 mm body lies from 221 mm to 371 mm. The 90 mm diameter is the smallest that holds the kit on the belly.

deriv.name: Full size newborn
deriv.why: The skin that packs into the folded volume at the packing of the full size study (silicone 47 percent of the folded volume): 0.173 m2. Kresling stories (n = 16, twist 22.6 degrees a story) open the length, sixteen star pleats open the girth, a 25 percent stretch pulls the creases smooth. Unfolding at about 300 Pa (estimate), full at 1344 Pa.

deriv.name: Tail end of the newborn
deriv.value: a neck of 40 mm radius for the first 129 mm
deriv.why: At full reach the valve is 74 mm short of the lip. The part of the body still inside must pass the opening while the nozzle holds the valve, so the first three stories stay narrow: the newborn has a tail as well.

deriv.name: Gel bowl
deriv.value: 5.37 L of gel in a bowl of 5.81 L, surface at 104 mm
deriv.why: One rounded bowl in the lower body, 304 mm long and 146 mm across at the axis of the print, with a flat top at the gel surface that runs on as the lip. The front holds the folded print (150 x 90 mm) with 5 mm of gel over the top; the keel starts to rise right under the nose of the print and reaches the lip 48 mm further on. The rear runs 67 mm back past the docking plane, under the rack in the tail, so the stems of the parked modules and the kit store stand in the gel and no tool has to cross a wall; the base of the arm stops the bowl there. The bowl is wide enough at the floor for the kit (50 mm) to pass. This costs gel: 5.37 L against 3.0 L for a bowl that ends at the docking plane.

deriv.name: Docking plane
deriv.value: 162 mm ahead of the arm axis, a thin 4 mm ring, three magnets, a silicone cord
deriv.why: The plane stands just ahead of the rack, so the rack, the tools and the kit store are all in the tail print and the gel chamber print is a bare shell. The seam therefore crosses the gel bowl, 67 mm of the bowl belong to the tail. The tail docks in the dry tank and the gel goes in before the water; three DC2-N52 disc magnets on steel discs (161 N) press a silicone cord in the ring. Once water and gel are in, the gel stands only 19 mm higher than the water, 186 Pa at the seam, and the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa) closes any gap under 1.1 mm.

deriv.name: Rack and kit store
deriv.value: in the tail, 150 mm ahead of the arm axis, 24 degrees to each side
deriv.why: Close to its base the DexArm holds the wrist at 134 mm and no higher, so a module hangs with the head 112 mm above the floor, the cup at 57 mm and the needle tip at 12 mm. No wall can stand between such a tool and the print, so the gel bowl runs back under the rack: the stems hang in the gel (surface 104 mm) and travel through the gel to the print. Each fork is two prongs printed with the tail, 4 mm above the gel, open to the front: the bare quick release comes up behind the module (33 mm of travel), clicks on, and slides the module forward out of the fork. The arm folds and unfolds through the 74 mm between the two parked heads. The kit store is three bumps on the floor of the bowl under the pneumatic module, which waits with the cup on the kit. Variants that failed: a rack beside the arm (base turned 90 to 110 degrees) needs the tool to cross the rim of the bowl, 114 mm high, with the needle tip at 12 mm; lifting the tool over the rim needs the tool 243 mm from the axis, which is outside the 308 mm wide tail when turned to the side; a raised base does not fit under the 336 mm roof (the folded arm is 314 mm tall).

deriv.name: Opening
deriv.value: lip 399 mm from the arm axis, 107 mm high; 214 x 250 mm; face leaning back 20 degrees
deriv.why: The lip continues the line of the gel surface, as drawn: 3 mm above the gel (the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm) and 22 mm above the water, so no water comes in and no gel runs out. The lip is as close to the arm as the print allows, because the nozzle reaches only 325 mm from the axis at the height of the valve. The lower half passes the newborn; the upper half gives the module head room at full reach.

deriv.name: Gel chamber
deriv.value: 240 x 314 x 336 mm outside, a bare shell
deriv.why: The front of the bowl, the opening and three seat bumps for the kit, printed in one piece with nothing to fit afterwards. Length from the docking plane to the lip, which the reach of the arm sets. One print on the H2S, docking face down, 100, 6 and 4 mm clear.

deriv.name: Water
deriv.why: Deep enough for the newborn with ballast (draft 45 mm) with 43 mm under the belly; low enough to stay 22 mm under the lip and 29 mm under the docking seam.

deriv.name: Time
deriv.why: First gel fill 54 min at 0.1 L per minute (micro peristaltic pump; later cycles only top up), print 39 min for 40 m of bead at 20 mm per second, cure 75 min, air about 96 s for 11.3 L: the inflator adds 55 kPa to a 7.6 L basketball in 35 s, so 7.6 x 55 / 101 = 4.1 L of free air in 35 s, 7.1 L per minute.

deriv.name: Tail contents
deriv.value: 8 parts, 0.82 kg, in two printed pockets
deriv.why: Cut to what one cycle needs, with the parts of the artist. Air: the CaRSun cordless inflator, 75 x 60 x 32 mm, with a battery of its own. Valve: the medical three way stopcock. Controller: the Raspberry Pi 5. Battery for the arm, the controller and the small pumps: about 25 Wh a cycle (arm 12 W while moving, estimate), six 18650 cells hold 54 Wh. Gel: one micro peristaltic pump; no gel store, the gel stays in the bowl. Silicone: two bores of the print with pistons, 96 mL for the 75 mL of one newborn. Vacuum for the cup: one micro pump, proposed. The newborn carries a ball inflation valve, and the nozzle on the arm is a ball inflation needle. The two FIT0800 water pumps stay in the kit of the newborn. The pockets are swellings of the side walls beside the arm, 56 mm deep, printed with the tail.

deriv.name: Printing the two parts
deriv.why: Tail: 286 x 314 x 336 mm in print orientation, about 1.7 kg of clear PETG at a 3 mm wall with the pockets and the rack, about 21 h at 18 mm3 per second. Gel chamber: 240 x 314 x 336 mm, about 1.1 kg, about 14 h. Both stand on the docking face, so the domes close without tall supports; the rack forks and the kit shelf need supports that break off. The fallback is not needed: each part in two blocks, split on the horizontal plane at half height, with a 6 mm tongue and groove and a solvent weld.

verdict.point: Two printed parts, tail and gel chamber, each in one piece on the H2S
verdict.why: Tail 286 x 314 x 336 mm, gel chamber 240 x 314 x 336 mm, against 340 x 320 x 340 mm.

verdict.point: Docking face with magnets, thin ring
verdict.why: Three disc magnets, 161 N, on a 4 mm ring. The seam now crosses the gel bowl, so the ring carries a silicone cord and the tail docks before the water comes in.

verdict.point: The shell of the gel chamber holds the gel in its lower part
verdict.why: 5.37 L, surface at 104 mm, held by one rounded bowl whose rim is 114 mm high all round, lower only at the lip.

verdict.point: DexArm on a fixed base in the tail, no boom, no rail; folds back, unfolds to work
verdict.why: Axis 162 mm behind the docking plane; the folded arm ends 65 mm behind the plane; all 2304 poses of the timeline are inside the joint ranges.

verdict.point: The arm as drawn: a tower, then two long links over the top of the docking face
verdict.why: The tower of the DexArm already contains the upper arm: the shoulder is 127 mm above the base and each link is 150 mm. The wrist reaches 282 mm above the floor at most, and only close to the base; at the far end of the print the wrist is at 211 mm.

verdict.point: One opening, on a slant at the upper front, thin plain rim, no magnets
verdict.ok: yes, lower and less slanted than drawn
verdict.why: The lip is at 107 mm, on the line of the gel surface, and the face leans back 20 degrees. The nozzle on the fixed arm reaches 176 mm high at 325 mm from the axis and no further, so the opening has to come to the arm.

verdict.point: Equipment behind the arm in the tail
verdict.ok: changed: beside the arm, inside the print
verdict.why: The parts are cut to 0.82 kg (battery 54 Wh, the inflator, the stopcock, the Raspberry Pi 5, a micro gel pump, a micro vacuum pump, two silicone bores) and sit in two pockets printed into the side walls. Nothing stands behind the arm, so the tail is 286 mm long instead of 336 mm.

verdict.point: Gel bowl as drawn in orange: flat top that runs on as the lip
verdict.why: The lip is 3 mm above the gel surface and 22 mm above the water.

verdict.point: Gel bowl as drawn: the rear bulges back past the docking seam
verdict.why: The rear of the bowl is part of the tail print and lies under the rack; the base of the arm stops the bowl. The seam crosses the gel and is sealed.

verdict.point: Gel bowl as drawn: the front curves up well before the nose, a shorter bowl
verdict.why: The print cannot move toward the arm: the needle reaches no nearer than 91 mm at the axis of the print, the folded newborn is 150 mm long, and the nose needs 28 mm to the lip. The keel already starts to rise under the nose of the print, at x 236 mm; the bowl ends at x 284 mm. A shorter bowl needs a shorter print, which means a smaller newborn.

verdict.point: Tool modules, tool changes and the kit store in the tail
verdict.why: Rack and kit store are 150 mm ahead of the arm axis, 4 mm behind the docking plane, part of the tail print. The stems hang in the rear of the gel bowl, so no tool crosses a wall. The gel chamber print carries no rack, no shelf and no insert.

verdict.point: The parent body rests on the tank floor; only the newborn floats
verdict.why: In 88 mm of water the tail weighs 8.0 kg (with steel ballast under the arm base where needed) against 6.5 kg of buoyancy, the filled gel chamber 4.6 kg against 3.1 kg; the empty gel chamber is held down by the docked tail.

verdict.point: The newborn grows to about the size of the gel chamber
verdict.why: Printed 150 x 90 mm, full size 395 x 280 mm: 165 percent of the length and 89 percent of the width of the gel chamber, 75 percent of the length of the whole parent body. The limit is the skin that packs into a print the arm can reach.

verdict.point: Birth by pushing while inflating, all air through the arm
verdict.why: The nozzle steers the tail end from above; the body slides over the lip; peak force 1.96 N of 4.91 N. A vertical tool cannot pull the body up a ramp, so the gel carries the body inside and the lip and the water carry the body outside.

limits: Open questions on the parts of the artist: the inflator gives pressure only, so the suction cup needs a vacuum source (one micro pump is proposed); the stopcock is manual (a micro servo on the lever, or set by hand); a tire inflator may not stop as low as 1.3 kPa; the product pages of the inflator, the stopcock and the ball valve were read by the artist and the coordinator, not opened from here.

Estimates, to measure: the mass of the DexArm (2.4 kg), the power of the DexArm while moving (12 W), the mass of the inflator and the size of the stopcock, the size of the micro pumps beyond the published figures, the module head (30 x 40 x 52 mm), the seal of the cup, the flow of gel through a 3.5 mm tube, the pressure that opens the folds (300 Pa), the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), the pump curve of the kit pumps, friction at the lip (0.2).

How the official joint angles J1 and J2 map onto the link meshes is an assumption, as on the full version. The DexArm specification page could not be opened again from here on 21 November 2026; its numbers are those used on the full version.

The valve is a soft boss on the tail cap and the nozzle stays vertical while the body pitches by up to 36 degrees: this needs a bench test. So does the drain of the gel from the folds, and whether a fold packed this tightly prints and opens as drawn.
The force on the valve is a quasi static estimate from slices: weight, buoyancy in the gel and in the water, the lip with friction, yield drag.

The newborn is drawn rigid with one soft droop where the body leaves the opening; a real skin at 300 Pa also wrinkles. In the force estimate the unfolded part outside is limp at that droop: the lip, the hull front and the water carry that part, and the arm steers only the part still inside. Friction at the gel wet lip is taken as 0.2.
The swim is a straight run on both jets and one slow turn; the speed comes from an estimated pump curve.
Overlap is measured from sampled points (4 to 11 mm apart) against exact surfaces, so a figure can be about 1 mm off.

read.birth_text: Quasi static estimate from slices. Peak 1.96 N; the payload of the DexArm is 4.91 N. The nozzle pushes forward and down; the gel carries the body inside, the lip and the water carry the body outside.
read.tank_text: The tank is the Ultum Nature Systems UNS 150U, a rimless low iron glass tank of 1500 x 600 x 600 mm with 15 mm glass (the longest stock length under 1.8 m; no stock tank is 1.3 m). The parent body, 526 mm long and 336 mm tall, stands on the floor at one end; 88 mm of water (64 L) leave the lip of the opening 22 mm above the water and give the newborn 786 mm of open water ahead. Filled as shown the tank weighs about 198 kg.
